chapters.name: 第七章 建筑的雕饰与装修

sections.name: 一、大木作雕饰
sections.content_zh:
老街上的建筑装饰，主要以木雕为主，石雕和砖雕的应用并不普遍。彩画虽然曾经被广泛应用在砖墙的檐下，但是能历经风雨保留下来的却很少。祠堂里的大木雕饰使用范围广泛，而且通常都非常精美。但是由于祠堂的主要空间均开敞，所以小木装修仅在厢房上才会使用，多数比较简单。住宅中的精美木雕主要位于门、窗、栏杆等处，部分住宅中的"马腿"、插叶、梁下巴等小型大木构件也雕饰得独具匠心、美轮美奂。

老街上过去由于家家都在忙着做香客的生意，所以没有什么匠人，过去盖房子需要的匠人都要从东阳请。解放后日子困难了，老街上的男孩子们才开始背井离乡出门学手艺，而这其中又以铁匠居多。老街上现在只有一位做大木的木匠，叫程高明（1942年生，第22代，圣字辈）。

马腿

"马腿"即江南民居中通常所说的"牛腿"，它位于檐柱上方，向天井垂直出挑。"马腿"的下半部分固定在马腿垫和檐柱上，用以承托上面的金枋。

金枋一般分为两部分，后面一段雕饰比较简单，通常只沿轮廓做几道线脚，内部辅以花卉题材为主的浅浮雕。但是这里也可以作为精雕细琢的重点，程昭夫祠堂中的部分金枋两侧就雕有生动的人物故事，绍常祠堂的一些金枋上则雕有三维的亭台楼阁。金枋尽端一般都有一个和金枋截面大小相当的一组三维人物或鸟兽，它们通常呈向庭院内伸展或端望的态势。金枋上面是金枋垫，上面承载着平行于立面的叠拱和沿进深方向的插叶。如果叠拱或插叶采用卷草纹造型，则金枋垫下面的这部分金枋垫还会做成花篮形状，使整个构件更为生动统一。

通体透雕的"马腿"可以说是整幢建筑中最精美的一块木雕。这个构件基本上只是对金枋起到一个斜撑的作用，所以它的上半部分，甚至整块木雕都可以和后面的柱子脱离，富于想象的匠人便利用到了这个特点，因地制宜地把部分雕刻内容也"转"到了"马腿"的背面。这样一来整组雕刻便显得更为生动，特别是对于雕有一组人物故事的"马腿"，如此处理后还增加了人物的立体感。这不禁让人想到希腊神庙三角山墙上的人物石雕，这种群雕的最大特点之一就是所有人物的姿态，以及人与人之间的相互关系，都能自然贴合屋顶的斜线，于是每一组山墙上的群雕都成了雕塑构图中的精品。比起希腊神庙三角山墙上的石雕，雕"马腿"的难度就要大多了。不仅所有的雕刻内容要控制在一个厚度单一的倒楔形体内，而且还要照顾到从正面和两侧三个面的视觉效果。由于人的视线较低，所以"马腿"的设计还会利用楔形的这个斜面和下面的观望者产生一种交流。

简单一点的"马腿"会雕"三狮戏球"，类似的母题一般用于祠堂中榀的两个檐柱上。世远公祠里的"马腿"是以一头成年狮子作为木雕的主体，它前腿着地，后腿高抬，守着眼前的绣球；它毛发冲天，略微低头，虎视眈眈地注视着下面的来访者。两只小狮子则在"马腿"整体空间构成的"空隙"中玩耍嬉戏，其实从某种意义上来讲，小狮子的位置和姿态才是设计的难点。

复杂的"马腿"会雕一组人物，并辅以相应的背景。程昭夫祠堂正堂中榀前檐柱上的"马腿"，一边是"王母骑凤"下凡，另一边是"玉皇大帝乘龙"到人间，跟随他们俩的还各有七个和五个辅助人物，分别是侍女、随从、天兵天将等人。王母和玉皇大帝等主要人物均面向中间，并稍适低头；他们身后还各有一个天兵驻守在"马腿"的另一侧，左盼右顾；更让人不禁拍案叫绝的是，在"马腿"的外下角，各有两个侍从，或低头、或坐、或弯腰、或俯身，似乎在暗自体察凡界中的冷暖是非。这些人物造型，个个都精雕细琢，惟妙惟肖；人物和人物之间主次分明，空间层次清楚。更难得的是，整组雕刻不但在立面上形成一个倒楔形，而且全部人物都控制在一个十多厘米的厚度里。

马腿垫上的雕饰一般比较简单，通常沿替木外围勾勒出一些线脚，内部浅雕花卉，或刻上诸如福、禄、寿之类的吉祥字眼，有的则是用几个"马腿"上的替木组成一句四字成语。

随着"马腿"的装饰性越来越大，它的设计也越来越灵活。在很多情况下，马腿垫和"马腿"可以简化为一块木头，只是在靠下的部分做了一个木楔子，插到柱子里。这样做的好处是在设计上可以比较自由，而且又多了一个面可以发挥匠人的创造性。程昭夫祠堂天井角部两个"马腿"的雕刻主题均为"仙人骑鱼"，鱼头向下，做纵身跃起状。"马腿"下原有的垫木在这里演化成了翻滚的浪花，如此一来，"鱼跃龙门"的态势便更加栩栩如生。胡公庙里的"盘龙马腿"则是用统一的图案把金枋、"马腿"和马腿垫连成一体，金枋雕龙头，"马腿"为龙身，马腿垫和后面的短梁化成彩云，整个"马腿"浑然一体，颇具匠心。

梭梁

梭梁的中部微微向上拱起，形如月亮，所以也被称为月梁。梭梁被普遍使用在祠堂的主要开敞空间里，还有部分住宅的檐廊下，甚至是厅堂里。梭梁上的雕饰并不多，基本只是集中在梁头两侧的"寥寥几刀"。但是不得不承认，不论是梭梁两侧弧形的截面，还是它两端卷杀的本身，就已经是绝美的雕刻作品。

梭梁两端卷杀的部分又被称作气堂，这里气堂上的雕饰有几种不同的做法。最简单的就是在梭梁两端雕上三道凹槽，这三条曲线仿佛是有弹性的梭梁在受力时形成的"褶皱"。雕饰讲究的建筑，或是跨度大一点的梭梁，凹槽末端还会衔接上一小束浅浅的阳刻卷草纹饰。这些纹饰紧紧地贴在梭梁尽端，仿佛是从柱子和梭梁的接缝中生长出来的。如果这样还不能尽兴，还可以在梁身上做文章。义丰雅记正堂中的五架梁，不但梭梁尽端的雕饰分外妖娆、极富装饰性，在凹槽的另外一侧又伸出一支更为舒展的卷草纹饰。程立重宅院一进院正堂中榀五架梁梁头的雕饰虽然比较简单，但是气堂内侧的卷草花纹则有半米多长。一些院落的檐下梭梁中部还雕有凤凰、蝙蝠、画卷、扇面等图案。

梭梁两端气堂的做法在不同时期也会略有不同。建造年代较早的建筑，如作勳公祠和世远公祠梭梁气堂中的凹槽较浅，凹槽和梭梁尽端阳刻卷草花纹的衔接也比较自然。相比而言，一百多年后建造的程昭夫祠堂中的梭梁，气堂的凹槽较深，其截面呈三角形，与阳刻卷草花纹的过渡也比较生硬，甚至凹槽本身的曲线也缺乏了那种柔韧之美，变得"硬邦邦"的。

梁下巴

梁下巴，即通常所说的梁托。它的雕刻通常比较程式化：在侧面沿轮廓刻一两道线脚，里面雕上一些简单的花卉，或是阳刻一个吉祥的字，大跨梁架下的梁下巴还可能在曲形底面上浅刻一些纹饰。老街上不论是祠堂还是住宅中的梁下巴大体都如此模式，唯独义丰南院正房檐廊下的四组梁下巴与众不同。这些梁下巴中的雕饰以城市或建筑为主题，并配有花草树木、人物鸟兽。这些建筑本身不但是三维立体的，而且建筑和其他事物之间的空间关系，在视觉上也表现得非常正确。这些梁下巴中所雕刻的建筑类型既有两进的农家小院，又有带长廊的深宅大院；既有小型的亭台楼阁，又有建筑在高台上的城楼殿宇；不仅如此，还有各式的拱桥和渔船若干。其雕刻的精细程度，更是让人叹为观止，三四厘米高的"房子"不但门、窗比例正确，而且可以看到屋面上的瓦线和屋檐下的雀替。就连通常只是一条凹槽的梁下巴轮廓线脚，在这里也变成了几十个紧密排列的"花瓣"。梁下巴的曲形底面上还深雕有精美菊花。

螰梁

程高明老人说，他不知道"转梁"中的"转"字如何写，只听人说"转"字代表一种动物，由此推断可能是"螰梁"。螰梁通常位于梁架结构靠上的部分，一端固定在柱子上，用来在纵向上牵引支撑桁条的叠拱。螰梁一般只在祠堂建筑中使用，老街上仅有绍常祠堂、程昭夫祠堂和周氏宗祠使用了这用螰梁。即便如此，这几幢建筑只有在最重要的空间，即正堂的梁架结构中才会使用到螰梁，由此可见其"级别"之高。在这三幢祠堂建筑中，绍常祠堂中的螰梁好似盘龙吐水，程昭夫祠堂里的也雕有一个龙头，只有周氏宗祠仅采用抽象的卷纹。

同一幢建筑中的螰梁造型相似，只是大小会根据桁条和桁条之间的距离做相应的调整。

程高明老人讲，通常如果用"三抽"，即三架梁，就不用螰梁。绍常祠堂正堂，中榀主要采用抬梁式结构，所以用"三抽"代替正脊下的螰梁。边榀则为穿斗结构，即采用螰梁而没有"三抽"。除此之外，每两个桁条或桁枋之间都有螰梁。每个盘龙形螰梁都接近一个圆形，龙身高高拱起，视觉上仿佛在支撑着上面的椽子，整个造型极富张力。龙身虽然向屋脊方向盘旋，但是龙头却高高昂起望向檐口，而且有五彩的水花从嘴里喷出。龙身由红、白、蓝、绿等颜色逐层退晕描画，龙身上还有彩绘花饰。

程昭夫祠堂的螰梁相对抽象，只能通过一双炯炯有神、望向地面的龙眼来确定整条龙的姿态。正堂中榀虽然也用了"三抽"，但是为了造型的统一，在"三抽"上依旧用螰梁做雕饰。这组螰梁已经没有结构作用，再加上"三抽"和椽子之间的空间矮小，所以这组螰梁的尾部向檐口方向旋绕，整体看上去好像"躺"了下来。

周氏宗祠里的螰梁在外形上与程昭夫祠堂里的螰梁相似，基本上都呈上大下小的椭圆形，但是它们没有了龙头，梁上的线脚也更为简洁，而且刻槽较浅，使得整个构件造型比较饱满，不乏质朴之美。

米梁、桁条、挑檐枋

米梁是指位于柱子之间的横向结构部件。桁条即檩子，如果截面接近方形也被称作桁枋。这些构件和挑檐枋都是主要的承重结构，一般不做任何雕饰，但是有些时候，这些构件的底面也会成为雕饰的载体。通常来说，这类雕饰只存在于祠堂建筑中，因为这里主要空间的梁架均露明，所以米梁、桁条和挑檐枋抬头可见。周氏宗祠拜厅天井一侧檐柱和金柱之间的米梁上都雕有浅浅的抽象的几何图案。程昭夫祠堂正堂的两个上金桁枋、前下金桁枋和檐枋，还有天井四周的挑檐枋底面都浮雕花草、凤凰、仙鹤、飞鸟、鱼纹和狮子戏球等图案。绍常祠堂在同样的位置也有雕饰：上金桁枋对称雕饰彩色勾连花卉；前下金桁枋和挑檐枋上各透雕一组花卉；檐枋上的透雕鱼纹、花鸟更是精美绝伦。据程高明老人讲，桁条一般都做成圆形，但是为了能在上面做雕饰，所以改成方形。雕饰的部分通常需要额外加上两层、甚至是三层木板，层数越多，越能雕出通透的感觉。

其他

雀替、叠拱、插叶、梁斗、梁斗垫、柱斗等部位也可以成为大木雕饰中的重点。叠拱和插叶是位于米梁、桁条或枋下面一组相互垂直的构件。支撑它们的可以是位于柱子上方的柱斗，也可以是位于梭梁上的梁斗。这些部位采用的雕饰母题多为卷草、花卉或抽象的回纹图案，有时候还会辅以寓意吉祥的字。
sections.content_en:
Architectural decoration on the old street is primarily wood carving, with stone carving and brick carving not commonly applied. Although painted decoration was once widely used under the eaves of brick walls, very little has survived the elements. Large wood carvings in ancestral halls have a wide range of applications and are usually very exquisite. However, because the main spaces of ancestral halls are all open, small wood joinery is only used on wing rooms, and most is relatively simple. Exquisite wood carvings in residences are mainly located at doors, windows, railings, and other places; some small large-timber components in residences such as "horse legs" (corbels), inserted leaves, and beam chins are also carved with unique ingenuity and breathtaking beauty.

In the past, because every family on the old street was busy doing business with pilgrims, there were few craftsmen; craftsmen needed for building houses in the past had to be hired from Dongyang. After liberation, when times became difficult, the boys on the old street began to leave their hometowns to learn trades, with blacksmiths being the majority. There is now only one carpenter doing large timber work on the old street, named Cheng Gaoming (born 1942, 22nd generation, Sheng character generation).

Horse Legs (Corbels)

The "horse leg" is what is commonly called "ox leg" in Jiangnan vernacular architecture; it is located above the eave column and projects vertically toward the courtyard. The lower part of the "horse leg" is fixed to the horse-leg pad and eave column, serving to support the golden beam above.

The golden beam is generally divided into two parts; the rear section has relatively simple carving, usually only a few molding lines along the outline, with shallow relief of floral themes inside. But this can also be a focus of meticulous carving: some golden beams in Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall have vivid human stories carved on both sides, while some golden beams in Shaochang Ancestral Hall are carved with three-dimensional pavilions and towers. The end of the golden beam generally has a group of three-dimensional human figures or birds and beasts comparable in size to the golden beam's cross-section, usually in poses extending toward the courtyard or gazing out. Above the golden beam is the golden-beam pad, which carries stacked brackets parallel to the facade and inserted leaves along the depth direction. If the stacked brackets or inserted leaves use scrolling grass patterns, the part of the golden-beam pad below will also be made into a flower basket shape, making the entire component more vivid and unified.

The fully openwork-carved "horse leg" can be said to be the most exquisite piece of wood carving in the entire building. This component basically only serves as a diagonal brace for the golden beam, so its upper half, even the entire wood carving, can be detached from the column behind; imaginative craftsmen took advantage of this feature, adapting to local conditions by "turning" part of the carving content to the back of the "horse leg." This makes the entire group of carvings more vivid, especially for "horse legs" carved with a group of human stories, which also increases the three-dimensionality of the figures after such treatment. This inevitably brings to mind the human figure stone carvings on the triangular pediments of Greek temples; one of the greatest features of such group carvings is that all figures' poses and the relationships between people can naturally conform to the sloping lines of the roof, so each group of pediment carvings becomes a masterpiece of sculptural composition. Compared to the stone carvings on Greek temple triangular pediments, carving a "horse leg" is much more difficult. Not only must all carving content be controlled within an inverted wedge-shaped body of uniform thickness, but also the visual effects from the front and both sides must be considered. Because people's line of sight is relatively low, the design of the "horse leg" also uses this sloped surface of the wedge to create a kind of communication with the viewer below.

Simpler "horse legs" are carved with "three lions playing with a ball"; similar motifs are generally used on the two eave columns of the central truss in ancestral halls. The "horse legs" in Shiyuan Ancestral Hall use an adult lion as the main subject of the wood carving, with its front legs on the ground and hind legs raised high, guarding the embroidered ball before it; its hair bristles upward, head slightly lowered, staring fiercely at the visitors below. Two small lions play and frolic in the "gaps" formed by the overall space of the "horse leg"; in a sense, the position and pose of the small lions are actually the难点 of the design.

Complex "horse legs" are carved with a group of human figures, supplemented by corresponding backgrounds. The "horse legs" on the front eave columns of the central truss in the main hall of Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall have "Queen Mother riding a phoenix" descending on one side and "Jade Emperor riding a dragon" coming to the human world on the other, with seven and five auxiliary figures respectively following them—maids, attendants, heavenly soldiers and generals, and others. The main figures such as the Queen Mother and Jade Emperor all face the center with slightly lowered heads; behind each there is also a heavenly soldier stationed on the other side of the "horse leg," looking left and right. What is even more breathtaking is that at the outer lower corners of the "horse legs," there are two attendants each—either bowing heads, sitting, bending waists, or leaning forward—seemingly quietly observing the warmth and cold, right and wrong of the mortal world. These figure models are all meticulously carved and lifelike; between figures, primary and secondary are distinct, and spatial layers are clear. What is even rarer is that the entire group of carvings not only forms an inverted wedge on the facade but also all figures are controlled within a thickness of just over ten centimeters.

The carving on the horse-leg pad is generally relatively simple, usually outlining some molding lines along the periphery of the substitute timber, with shallowly carved flowers inside, or auspicious characters such as fortune, prosperity, and longevity carved in relief; some use the substitute timbers on several "horse legs" to form a four-character idiom.

As the decorative nature of "horse legs" has grown, their design has become increasingly flexible. In many cases, the horse-leg pad and "horse leg" can be simplified into a single piece of wood, with only a wooden wedge made in the lower part to insert into the column. The advantage of this is greater design freedom and an additional surface for the craftsman's creativity. The carving theme of the two "horse legs" at the courtyard corners of Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall is both "immortal riding a fish," with the fish head downward in a leaping pose. The original pad timber below the "horse leg" here evolves into rolling waves, making the "fish leaping through the dragon gate" pose even more lifelike. The "coiled dragon horse leg" in Hugong Temple uses a unified pattern to integrate the golden beam, "horse leg," and horse-leg pad into one body: the golden beam is carved as a dragon head, the "horse leg" as the dragon body, and the horse-leg pad and short beam behind transform into colorful clouds, making the entire "horse leg" a seamless whole with considerable ingenuity.

Shuttle Beams

The middle of a shuttle beam arches slightly upward, shaped like a moon, hence also called a moon beam. Shuttle beams are commonly used in the main open spaces of ancestral halls, under the eave corridors of some residences, and even in halls. There is not much carving on shuttle beams, basically concentrated in just "a few strokes" on both sides of the beam head. But it must be admitted that whether it is the curved cross-section on both sides of the shuttle beam or the entasis at both ends itself, it is already a stunning carving work.

The entasis parts at both ends of the shuttle beam are also called qi tang (air hall); there are several different approaches to carving here. The simplest is to carve three grooves at both ends of the shuttle beam; these three curves seem like "wrinkles" formed when the elastic shuttle beam is under load. In buildings with elaborate carving, or shuttle beams with larger spans, the ends of the grooves will also connect to a small束 of shallow relief scrolling grass ornamentation. These ornamentation cling tightly to the ends of the shuttle beam, as if growing out from the joints between columns and shuttle beams. If this is still not enough, one can also work on the beam body. The five-purlin beam in the main hall of Yifeng Yaji not only has particularly enchanting and highly decorative carving at the shuttle beam ends, but also extends a more舒展 scrolling grass ornamentation on the other side of the groove. Although the carving at the beam head of the five-purlin beam on the central truss of the main hall in the first courtyard of Cheng Lizhong's residence is relatively simple, the scrolling grass pattern on the inner side of the qi tang is over half a meter long. The middle of shuttle beams under the eaves of some courtyards is also carved with patterns such as phoenixes, bats, painting scrolls, and fans.

The approach to qi tang at both ends of shuttle beams also varies slightly in different periods. In buildings of earlier construction dates, such as Zuoxun Gong Ancestral Hall and Shiyuan Gong Ancestral Hall, the grooves in the shuttle beam qi tang are shallower, and the connection between the grooves and the relief scrolling grass patterns at the shuttle beam ends is also more natural. In comparison, the shuttle beams in Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall built over a hundred years later have deeper qi tang grooves with triangular cross-sections, and the transition to relief scrolling grass patterns is also more rigid; even the curves of the grooves themselves lack that flexible beauty, becoming "stiff."

 Beam Chins

The beam chin, commonly known as the beam bracket. Its carving is usually quite formulaic: one or two molding lines carved along the outline on the side, with some simple flowers carved inside, or an auspicious character in relief; beam chins under large-span beam frames may also have shallowly carved ornamentation on the curved bottom surface. Whether in ancestral halls or residences on the old street, beam chins generally follow this pattern—except for the four groups of beam chins under the eave corridor of the main house in the south courtyard of Yifeng, which are与众不同. The carvings in these beam chins take cities or architecture as themes, supplemented with flowers, plants, trees, human figures, birds, and beasts. These buildings themselves are not only three-dimensional but also the spatial relationships between buildings and other things are visually represented very correctly. The types of architecture carved in these beam chins include both two-courtyard farmsteads and deep mansions with long corridors; both small pavilions and towers and city gate towers and palace halls built on high platforms; moreover, there are various arched bridges and fishing boats. The fineness of their carving is even more breathtaking: the "houses" only three or four centimeters high not only have correct door and window proportions but also show tile lines on the roof and sparrow brackets under the eaves. Even the beam chin contour molding, usually just a single groove, here becomes dozens of closely arranged "petals." The curved bottom surface of the beam chin is also deeply carved with exquisite chrysanthemums.

 Cicada Beams

Elder Cheng Gaoming says he does not know how to write the "zhuan" character in "zhuan beam," only hearing that the character represents an animal, from which it is inferred it may be "cicada beam." Cicada beams are usually located in the upper part of the beam frame structure, with one end fixed to the column, used to longitudinally牵引 and support the stacked brackets of purlins. Cicada beams are generally only used in ancestral hall architecture; only Shaochang Ancestral Hall, Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall, and Zhou Family Ancestral Hall on the old street use cicada beams. Even so, these buildings only use cicada beams in the most important space—the beam frame structure of the main hall—showing how high their "status" is. Among these three ancestral hall buildings, the cicada beam in Shaochang Ancestral Hall resembles a coiled dragon spitting water, the one in Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall is also carved with a dragon head, and only Zhou Family Ancestral Hall uses abstract scrolling patterns.

Cicada beams in the same building have similar shapes, with only the size adjusted accordingly based on the distance between purlins.

Elder Cheng Gaoming says that usually if "three chou" (three-purlin beams) are used, cicada beams are not used. In the main hall of Shaochang Ancestral Hall, the central truss mainly adopts the post-and-lintel (tailiang) structure, so "three chou" replaces the cicada beam under the main ridge. The side trusses use the column-and-tie (chuandou) structure, i.e., using cicada beams without "three chou." In addition, there are cicada beams between every two purlins or purlin beams. Each coiled-dragon-shaped cicada beam is nearly circular, with the dragon body arched high, visually seeming to support the rafters above, and the entire shape is full of tension. Although the dragon body coils toward the ridge direction, the dragon head is raised high looking toward the eave, with colorful water spray erupting from its mouth. The dragon body is painted with layered color gradients of red, white, blue, green, and other colors, and there are also painted floral decorations on the dragon body.

The cicada beams in Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall are relatively abstract, and the posture of the entire dragon can only be determined through a pair of bright, piercing dragon eyes gazing toward the ground. Although the central truss of the main hall also uses "three chou," for the unity of造型, cicada beams are still used for carving decoration on the "three chou." This group of cicada beams no longer has a structural function; coupled with the small space between the "three chou" and the rafters, the tails of this group of cicada beams coil toward the eave direction, and the whole looks as if it has "lain down."

The cicada beams in Zhou Family Ancestral Hall are similar in外形 to those in Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall, basically all呈 oval shapes larger at the top and smaller at the bottom, but they lack dragon heads, the molding lines on the beams are also simpler, and the carved grooves are shallower, making the entire component造型 relatively full, not lacking in rustic beauty.

Mi Beams, Purlins, and Eave-Picking Beams

Mi beams refer to the horizontal structural components located between columns. Purlins (桁条) are also called rafter beams; if their cross-section is nearly square, they are also called purlin beams (桁枋). These components and eave-picking beams (挑檐枋) are all primary load-bearing structures and generally have no carving, but sometimes the bottom surfaces of these components can also become carriers for carving decoration. Generally speaking, this type of carving only exists in ancestral hall architecture, because the beam frames in the main spaces here are all exposed, so mi beams, purlins, and eave-picking beams are visible when looking up. Shallow abstract geometric patterns are carved on the mi beams between the eave columns and golden columns on one side of the courtyard in the worship hall of Zhou Family Ancestral Hall. The bottom surfaces of the two upper golden purlin beams, front lower golden purlin beams, and eave beams in the main hall of Cheng Zhaofu Ancestral Hall, as well as the eave-picking beams around the courtyard, are all relief-carved with patterns such as flowers and plants, phoenixes, cranes, flying birds, fish patterns, and lions playing with balls. Shaochang Ancestral Hall also has carvings in the same positions: the upper golden purlin beams are symmetrically decorated with colored interlocking flowers; the front lower golden purlin beams and eave-picking beams each have a group of openwork-carved flowers; the openwork-carved fish patterns and flower-and-bird designs on the eave beams are even more exquisite. According to Elder Cheng Gaoming, purlins are generally made circular, but to enable carving on them, they are changed to square. The carved part usually requires adding two or even three extra layers of wood boards; the more layers, the more transparent the carving can be.

Other Components

Sparrow brackets (雀替), stacked brackets (叠拱), inserted leaves (插叶), beam dou (梁斗), beam dou pads (梁斗垫), and column dou (柱斗) can also become key points in large wood carving decoration. Stacked brackets and inserted leaves are a group of mutually perpendicular components located below mi beams, purlins, or beams. What supports them can be column dou located above columns, or beam dou located on shuttle beams. The carving motifs used in these parts are mostly scrolling grass, flowers, or abstract key-fret patterns, sometimes supplemented with auspicious characters.
key_terms: 老街上的建筑装饰主要以木雕为主石雕和砖雕的应用并不普遍
彩画虽然曾经被广泛应用在砖墙的檐下但是能历经风雨保留下来的却很少
祠堂里的大木雕饰使用范围广泛而且通常都非常精美
由于祠堂的主要空间均开敞所以小木装修仅在厢房上才会使用多数比较简单
住宅中的精美木雕主要位于门窗栏杆等处部分住宅中的马腿插叶梁下巴等小型大木构件也雕饰得独具匠心美轮美奂
老街上过去由于家家都在忙着做香客的生意所以没有什么匠人过去盖房子需要的匠人都要从东阳请
解放后日子困难了老街上的男孩子们才开始背井离乡出门学手艺而这其中又以铁匠居多
老街上现在只有一位做大木的木匠叫程高明1942年生第22代圣字辈
马腿即江南民居中通常所说的牛腿它位于檐柱上方向天井垂直出挑
马腿的下半部分固定在马腿垫和檐柱上用以承托上面的金枋
金枋一般分为两部分后面一段雕饰比较简单通常只沿轮廓做几道线脚内部辅以花卉题材为主的浅浮雕
程昭夫祠堂中的部分金枋两侧就雕有生动的人物故事绍常祠堂的一些金枋上则雕有三维的亭台楼阁
金枋尽端一般都有一个和金枋截面大小相当的一组三维人物或鸟兽它们通常呈向庭院内伸展或端望的态势
金枋上面是金枋垫上面承载着平行于立面的叠拱和沿进深方向的插叶
如果叠拱或插叶采用卷草纹造型则金枋垫下面的这部分金枋垫还会做成花篮形状使整个构件更为生动统一
通体透雕的马腿可以说是整幢建筑中最精美的一块木雕
马腿基本上只是对金枋起到一个斜撑的作用所以它的上半部分甚至整块木雕都可以和后面的柱子脱离富于想象的匠人便利用到了这个特点因地制宜地把部分雕刻内容也转到了马腿的背面
这样一来整组雕刻便显得更为生动特别是对于雕有一组人物故事的马腿如此处理后还增加了人物的立体感
这不禁让人想到希腊神庙三角山墙上的人物石雕这种群雕的最大特点之一就是所有人物的姿态以及人与人之间的相互关系都能自然贴合屋顶的斜线于是每一组山墙上的群雕都成了雕塑构图中的精品
比起希腊神庙三角山墙上的石雕雕马腿的难度就要大多了不仅所有的雕刻内容要控制在一个厚度单一的倒楔形体内而且还要照顾到从正面和两侧三个面的视觉效果
由于人的视线较低所以马腿的设计还会利用楔形的这个斜面和下面的观望者产生一种交流
简单一点的马腿会雕三狮戏球类似的母题一般用于祠堂中榀的两个檐柱上
世远公祠里的马腿是以一头成年狮子作为木雕的主体它前腿着地后腿高抬守着眼前的绣球它毛发冲天略微低头虎视眈眈地注视着下面的来访者
两只小狮子则在马腿整体空间构成的空隙中玩耍嬉戏其实从某种意义上来讲小狮子的位置和姿态才是设计的难点
复杂的马腿会雕一组人物并辅以相应的背景
程昭夫祠堂正堂中榀前檐柱上的马腿一边是王母骑凤下凡另一边是玉皇大帝乘龙到人间跟随他们俩的还各有七个和五个辅助人物分别是侍女随从天兵天将等人
王母和玉皇大帝等主要人物均面向中间并稍适低头他们身后还各有一个天兵驻守在马腿的另一侧左盼右顾
在马腿的外下角各有两个侍从或低头或坐或弯腰或俯身似乎在暗自体察凡界中的冷暖是非
这些人物造型个个都精雕细琢惟妙惟肖人物和人物之间主次分明空间层次清楚
整组雕刻不但在立面上形成一个倒楔形而且全部人物都控制在一个十多厘米的厚度里
马腿垫上的雕饰一般比较简单通常沿替木外围勾勒出一些线脚内部浅雕花卉或刻上诸如福禄寿之类的吉祥字眼有的则是用几个马腿上的替木组成一句四字成语
随着马腿的装饰性越来越大它的设计也越来越灵活
在很多情况下马腿垫和马腿可以简化为一块木头只是在靠下的部分做了一个木楔子插到柱子里这样做的好处是在设计上可以比较自由而且又多了一个面可以发挥匠人的创造性
程昭夫祠堂天井角部两个马腿的雕刻主题均为仙人骑鱼鱼头向下做纵身跃起状马腿下原有的垫木在这里演化成了翻滚的浪花如此一来鱼跃龙门的态势便更加栩栩如生
胡公庙里的盘龙马腿则是用统一的图案把金枋马腿和马腿垫连成一体金枋雕龙头马腿为龙身马腿垫和后面的短梁化成彩云整个马腿浑然一体颇具匠心
梭梁的中部微微向上拱起形如月亮所以也被称为月梁
梭梁被普遍使用在祠堂的主要开敞空间里还有部分住宅的檐廊下甚至是厅堂里
梭梁上的雕饰并不多基本只是集中在梁头两侧的寥寥几刀但是不得不承认不论是梭梁两侧弧形的截面还是它两端卷杀的本身就已经是绝美的雕刻作品
梭梁两端卷杀的部分又被称作气堂这里气堂上的雕饰有几种不同的做法
最简单的就是在梭梁两端雕上三道凹槽这三条曲线仿佛是有弹性的梭梁在受力时形成的褶皱
雕饰讲究的建筑或是跨度大一点的梭梁凹槽末端还会衔接上一小束浅浅的阳刻卷草纹饰这些纹饰紧紧地贴在梭梁尽端仿佛是从柱子和梭梁的接缝中生长出来的
义丰雅记正堂中的五架梁不但梭梁尽端的雕饰分外妖娆极富装饰性在凹槽的另外一侧又伸出一支更为舒展的卷草纹饰
程立重宅院一进院正堂中榀五架梁梁头的雕饰虽然比较简单但是气堂内侧的卷草花纹则有半米多长
一些院落的檐下梭梁中部还雕有凤凰蝙蝠画卷扇面等图案
梭梁两端气堂的做法在不同时期也会略有不同
建造年代较早的建筑如作勳公祠和世远公祠梭梁气堂中的凹槽较浅凹槽和梭梁尽端阳刻卷草花纹的衔接也比较自然
一百多年后建造的程昭夫祠堂中的梭梁气堂的凹槽较深其截面呈三角形与阳刻卷草花纹的过渡也比较生硬甚至凹槽本身的曲线也缺乏了那种柔韧之美变得硬邦邦的
梁下巴即通常所说的梁托
梁下巴的雕刻通常比较程式化在侧面沿轮廓刻一两道线脚里面雕上一些简单的花卉或是阳刻一个吉祥的字大跨梁架下的梁下巴还可能在曲形底面上浅刻一些纹饰
老街上不论是祠堂还是住宅中的梁下巴大体都如此模式唯独义丰南院正房檐廊下的四组梁下巴与众不同
这些梁下巴中的雕饰以城市或建筑为主题并配有花草树木人物鸟兽
这些建筑本身不但是三维立体的而且建筑和其他事物之间的空间关系在视觉上也表现得非常正确
这些梁下巴中所雕刻的建筑类型既有两进的农家小院又有带长廊的深宅大院既有小型的亭台楼阁又有建筑在高台上的城楼殿宇不仅如此还有各式的拱桥和渔船若干
其雕刻的精细程度更是让人叹为观止三四厘米高的房子不但门窗比例正确而且可以看到屋面上的瓦线和屋檐下的雀替
就连通常只是一条凹槽的梁下巴轮廓线脚在这里也变成了几十个紧密排列的花瓣梁下巴的曲形底面上还深雕有精美菊花
程高明老人说他不知道转梁中的转字如何写只听人说转字代表一种动物由此推断可能是螰梁
螰梁通常位于梁架结构靠上的部分一端固定在柱子上用来在纵向上牵引支撑桁条的叠拱
螰梁一般只在祠堂建筑中使用老街上仅有绍常祠堂程昭夫祠堂和周氏宗祠使用了这用螰梁
这几幢建筑只有在最重要的空间即正堂的梁架结构中才会使用到螰梁由此可见其级别之高
在这三幢祠堂建筑中绍常祠堂中的螰梁好似盘龙吐水程昭夫祠堂里的也雕有一个龙头只有周氏宗祠仅采用抽象的卷纹
同一幢建筑中的螰梁造型相似只是大小会根据桁条和桁条之间的距离做相应的调整
程高明老人讲通常如果用三抽即三架梁就不用螰梁
绍常祠堂正堂中榀主要采用抬梁式结构所以用三抽代替正脊下的螰梁
边榀则为穿斗结构即采用螰梁而没有三抽
每两个桁条或桁枋之间都有螰梁
每个盘龙形螰梁都接近一个圆形龙身高高拱起视觉上仿佛在支撑着上面的椽子整个造型极富张力
龙身虽然向屋脊方向盘旋但是龙头却高高昂起望向檐口而且有五彩的水花从嘴里喷出
龙身由红白蓝绿等颜色逐层退晕描画龙身上还有彩绘花饰
程昭夫祠堂的螰梁相对抽象只能通过一双炯炯有神望向地面的龙眼来确定整条龙的姿态
正堂中榀虽然也用了三抽但是为了造型的统一在三抽上依旧用螰梁做雕饰
这组螰梁已经没有结构作用再加上三抽和椽子之间的空间矮小所以这组螰梁的尾部向檐口方向旋绕整体看上去好像躺了下来
周氏宗祠里的螰梁在外形上与程昭夫祠堂里的螰梁相似基本上都呈上大下小的椭圆形但是它们没有了龙头梁上的线脚也更为简洁而且刻槽较浅使得整个构件造型比较饱满不乏质朴之美
米梁是指位于柱子之间的横向结构部件
桁条即檩子如果截面接近方形也被称作桁枋
这些构件和挑檐枋都是主要的承重结构一般不做任何雕饰但是有些时候这些构件的底面也会成为雕饰的载体
这类雕饰只存在于祠堂建筑中因为这里主要空间的梁架均露明所以米梁桁条和挑檐枋抬头可见
周氏宗祠拜厅天井一侧檐柱和金柱之间的米梁上都雕有浅浅的抽象的几何图案
程昭夫祠堂正堂的两个上金桁枋前下金桁枋和檐枋还有天井四周的挑檐枋底面都浮雕花草凤凰仙鹤飞鸟鱼纹和狮子戏球等图案
绍常祠堂在同样的位置也有雕饰上金桁枋对称雕饰彩色勾连花卉前下金桁枋和挑檐枋上各透雕一组花卉檐枋上的透雕鱼纹花鸟更是精美绝伦
据程高明老人讲桁条一般都做成圆形但是为了能在上面做雕饰所以改成方形
雕饰的部分通常需要额外加上两层甚至是三层木板层数越多越能雕出通透的感觉
雀替叠拱插叶梁斗梁斗垫柱斗等部位也可以成为大木雕饰中的重点
叠拱和插叶是位于米梁桁条或枋下面一组相互垂直的构件
支撑它们的可以是位于柱子上方的柱斗也可以是位于梭梁上的梁斗
这些部位采用的雕饰母题多为卷草花卉或抽象的回纹图案有时候还会辅以寓意吉祥的字

sections.name: 二、小木作装修
sections.content_zh:
门、窗

老街上的住宅，正房明间通常有六扇通高并可摘除的门扇，以便在需要的时候，使正堂和明堂在空间上连成一体。除了正房明间以外，余下各间的门窗处理大体相同。每一开间被分为三部分：中间的一扇上面为窗，下面为板；左右两侧上面是高窗，下面为板，其中一侧板的三分之二可以开启为门。整体看起来对比强烈、重点突出，却又疏密有致、匀称均衡。可以说对于老街上大部分的住宅，每间正中的那扇窗就是整幢建筑中最为精美的一件木雕。两侧的高窗一般采用和主窗类似的雕刻主题，但会相对简洁。

以义丰雅记为例，早期住宅的窗子分为上下两屉。下屉窗的位置恰好在视线高度，面积较小，为固定窗。檐廊下常有人走动，做成固定窗，既不会影响房间里的人休息，又不会妨碍檐下的人走路。上屉窗为两扇平推窗，窗下檐高过一般人的头顶。每扇平推窗又会沿水平、垂直、水平方向上依次分格，每次分成比例匀称的小、大、小三部分，并雕以不同的纹饰。整扇窗结构、层次清楚，又重点突出。早期的窗花通常以抽象的几何回纹图案为主，线条匀称、构图大方。类似的回纹构图在附近村落同一时期的住宅里也可以看到。

十九世纪中期以后建造的住宅，上屉平推窗的尺寸在两个方向上都有所减小，三边余下的部分和下屉窗一起组成了一个大的窗套。平推窗本身只沿水平方向做一次划分，窗套的上半部分会再做两次到三次格，成为固定的雕花小窗。从雕饰的题材上来看，含有吉祥寓意的鸟兽、花草、字画，甚至是亭台楼阁等具象图案成为雕刻的主题和重点。这些图案通常位于每个分格的中间部位，四周衬以抽象纹饰。下屉固定窗的面积较大，通常还会嵌上三组这样的图案。用做背景的回纹也变得更为精致、细腻、富有层次，但同时却少了过去的那种朴素之美，略显矫揉造作。

栏板

老街上的早期建筑，可能由于二层原本并不住人，所以二层栏板不做任何雕饰，只是把十多厘米宽的木板竖向排列在栏板的框架之间。清末民初，由于车床的引进，带螺纹的木质栏杆成为一种时尚。对于大户有钱人家，这种千篇一律的机械式加工显然有失水准，所以便出现了手工雕刻的栏板。老街上有两幢中西合璧式木构单体"别墅"，新仁昌旅店和程铿别墅，每一幢都有精美的雕花栏板。这一方面可能是受到了西方建筑装饰的影响，更重要的是这两幢建筑的居住空间都不仅仅局限在一层，所以高层空间也就自然而然地产生了装饰装修的需求。

新仁昌旅店原为四层高单体建筑，现仅剩两层；建筑三开间，雕花栏板位于二层前廊。明间栏板分成三段，每段内有雕花栏板三块，每块约二十五厘米宽、七十厘米高，两块之间的间隔比栏板宽度略小；次间有同样大小的雕花栏板各十块，均匀排列。雕刻的主题大部分以吉祥鸟兽为主，并配以不同的花草，例如狮子、凤凰、仙鹤、鸳鸯、喜鹊、雄鸡等。其中明间正中的一组分别是凤凰、狮子、凤凰，并且两凤凰面面相觑。明间栏板的边框处理还和次间略有不同，两侧做竹节状线脚，并且相互间高低错落有致。这二十九块雕花栏板之中，有三块边框的处理手法不同，而且雕的都是姿态相同的白菜，推断是上层的栏板拆下来补缺的。余下的二十六块虽然有的采用相同的主题，但是个个造型独特。

程铿别墅高两层，宽三开间，进深两开间，二层四面有廊。每开间栏板分三组，每组三块；走廊进深这一架也有栏板三块。所有栏板都以回纹为底，镂空雕饰，栏板的宽度根据其所在的位置不同，稍有变化，宽度或位置一样的栏板采用相同的回纹样式。稍宽的栏板在回纹中间嵌雕有宝瓶、仙鹤、月季等图案。
sections.content_en:
Doors and Windows

In residences on the old street, the central bay (明间) of the main house usually has six full-height removable door panels, so that when needed, the main hall and the front hall can be spatially integrated. Except for the central bay of the main house, the door and window treatment of the remaining bays is generally the same. Each bay is divided into three parts: the central panel has a window above and a board below; the left and right sides have high windows above and boards below, with two-thirds of one side board openable as a door. The overall appearance has strong contrast and prominent focus, yet is well-proportioned and balanced. It can be said that for most residences on the old street, the central window of each bay is the most exquisite piece of wood carving in the entire building. The high windows on both sides generally use similar carving themes as the main window but are relatively simpler.

Taking Yifeng Yaji as an example, the windows of early residences are divided into upper and lower sashes. The lower sash window is positioned exactly at eye level, with a relatively small area, and is a fixed window. People often walk under the eave corridor, so making it a fixed window neither affects the rest of people in the room nor hinders people walking under the eaves. The upper sash consists of two sliding windows, with the lower eave of the window higher than an average person's head. Each sliding window is further divided sequentially along horizontal, vertical, and horizontal directions, each time divided into three proportionally balanced parts—small, large, small—and carved with different ornamentation. The entire window has clear structure and layers, with prominent focus. Early window patterns are usually dominated by abstract geometric key-fret patterns, with balanced lines and generous composition. Similar key-fret compositions can also be seen in residences of the same period in nearby villages.

In residences built after the mid-nineteenth century, the size of the upper sliding windows decreased in both directions, and the remaining parts on three sides together with the lower sash window formed a large window frame. The sliding window itself is only divided once along the horizontal direction, and the upper part of the window frame is further divided two to three times, becoming fixed carved small windows. In terms of carving themes, representational patterns with auspicious meanings—such as birds and beasts, flowers and plants, calligraphy and paintings, and even pavilions and towers—became the main themes and focus of carving. These patterns are usually located in the center of each division, surrounded by abstract ornamentation. The lower fixed window has a relatively large area and usually embeds three groups of such patterns. The key-fret patterns used as backgrounds also became more refined, delicate, and layered, but at the same time lost the simple beauty of the past, appearing somewhat contrived.

 Railing Panels

In early buildings on the old street, perhaps because the second floor was originally not for living, the second-floor railing panels had no carving decoration, only vertically arranged wooden boards over ten centimeters wide within the railing frame. In the late Qing and early Republican periods, due to the introduction of lathes, threaded wooden railings became fashionable. For wealthy families, this monotonous mechanical processing was clearly substandard, so hand-carved railing panels appeared. There are two Chinese-Western style wooden standalone "villas" on the old street—Xinrenchang Inn and Cheng Keng Villa—each with exquisite carved railing panels. On the one hand, this may have been influenced by Western architectural decoration; more importantly, the living spaces of these two buildings were not limited to the first floor, so the upper-level spaces naturally generated a demand for decoration and finishing.

Xinrenchang Inn was originally a four-story standalone building, now only two stories remain; the building is three bays wide, with carved railing panels on the second-floor front corridor. The central bay railing is divided into three sections, each containing three carved railing panels, each about twenty-five centimeters wide and seventy centimeters high, with the gap between two panels slightly smaller than the panel width; the side bays each have ten carved railing panels of the same size, evenly arranged. Most carving themes are auspicious birds and beasts, supplemented with different flowers and plants, such as lions, phoenixes, cranes, mandarin ducks, magpies, and roosters. Among them, the central group of the central bay is respectively phoenix, lion, phoenix, with the two phoenixes facing each other. The border treatment of the central bay railing is also slightly different from the side bays, with bamboo-joint-shaped molding on both sides, and mutually staggered heights. Among these twenty-nine carved railing panels, three have different border treatment methods and are all carved with cabbages in the same pose, inferred to be railing panels removed from the upper floor to fill gaps. The remaining twenty-six panels, although some use the same theme, each has a unique造型.

Cheng Keng Villa is two stories high, three bays wide, two bays deep, with corridors on all four sides of the second floor. Each bay's railing is divided into three groups, each with three panels; the corridor depth bay also has three railing panels. All railing panels use key-fret patterns as the base with openwork carving; the width of the railing panels varies slightly depending on their position, and panels of the same width or position use the same key-fret pattern. The slightly wider panels have embedded carvings of treasure vases, cranes, Chinese roses, and other patterns in the middle of the key-fret.

sections.name: 三、砖石雕
sections.content_zh:
老街上建筑中的石雕很少，主要用在柱础上。这里的柱础形制比较简单，除了祠堂正堂中间的几个柱础有覆盆之外，其余的皆为鼓形柱础。柱础一般不做雕饰，最多只在上下各做一道线脚。另一处用石雕的地方则在庭院的角落处。以程成昌旅店为例，明堂四角各有一个一尺见方的石板，中间雕成阴阳相间的铜钱纹样，这样雨水就可以从这里流到院落下面的雨水道，再汇入老街两侧的雨水沟，最终流入方岩溪。

砖雕主要应用在马头墙上，还有建筑正立面旁门上，或是小窗上的眉檐。眉檐的做法通常是下面有几排"砖牙子"，然后是仿木构的椽头，上面再加一两皮挑砖，砖上放瓦。"高级"一点的眉檐可以多砌几排"砖牙子"，也可以做两层椽头相叠。程振兴四合院入口上的眉檐，不仅挑了六层"砖牙子"，而且中间还外加收分，整个眉檐还用红、白、黑三色相间描画。

老街上唯一一幢立面上饰有大量砖雕或石雕的建筑是得耕居。得耕居的建造年代较早，采用牌楼式门楼。中间的重檐牌楼为砖砌仿木结构，上面不但用砖雕砌出梁、柱、枋、柱头、柱础、椽头等构件，而且还用砖雕模拟雀替和柱头上的雕饰，甚至是梁枋上的彩画，靠近檐口的部分砖雕还残留有彩绘的印记。砖雕的主题既有一些抽象的花纹，又包括一些精美的鱼纹和鸟兽。最精美的雕饰要属门额上方的"双狮抢球"石雕，门额正中砖刻"得耕居"三字，并在两侧辅以石雕麒麟，下方衬以砖雕花鸟。
sections.content_en:
Stone carvings in buildings on the old street are very few, mainly used on column bases. The column bases here are relatively simple in form; except for several column bases in the middle of the ancestral hall main hall that have inverted basins, the rest are all drum-shaped column bases. Column bases generally have no carving decoration, at most only one molding line on the top and bottom each. Another place using stone carving is at the corners of the courtyard. Taking Cheng Chengchang Inn as an example, each of the four corners of the front hall has a one-chi-square stone slab, with the middle carved into alternating yin-yang copper coin patterns, so that rainwater can flow from here into the rainwater channel below the courtyard, then into the rainwater ditches on both sides of the old street, and finally into Fangyan Stream.

Brick carving is mainly applied on horse-head walls, as well as on side doors of building front facades, or on the eyebrow eaves above small windows. The usual practice for eyebrow eaves is to have several rows of "brick teeth" below, followed by imitation wooden rafter heads, then one or two courses of projecting bricks above, with tiles placed on the bricks. More "高级" eyebrow eaves can have more rows of "brick teeth" built, or two layers of overlapping rafter heads. The eyebrow eave above the entrance of Cheng Zhenxing's courtyard house not only projects six layers of "brick teeth" but also has additional entasis in the middle, with the entire eyebrow eave painted in alternating red, white, and black colors.

The only building on the old street with a large amount of brick or stone carving on its facade is Degeng Residence. Degeng Residence was built relatively early and adopts a paifang-style gatehouse. The central double-eave paifang is a brick imitation wooden structure, on which not only are components such as beams, columns, beams, column heads, column bases, and rafter heads carved from brick, but also brick carvings simulate sparrow brackets and carvings on column heads, and even painted decoration on beams; the brick carvings near the eave still retain traces of colored painting. The themes of brick carving include both abstract patterns and exquisite fish patterns and birds and beasts. The most exquisite carving is the "two lions grabbing a ball" stone carving above the door lintel; the center of the door lintel has the three characters "Degeng Residence" carved in brick, flanked by stone-carved qilin on both sides, with brick-carved flowers and birds below.

另一处用石雕的地方则在庭院的角落处
以程成昌旅店为例明堂四角各有一个一尺见方的石板中间雕成阴阳相间的铜钱纹样这样雨水就可以从这里流到院落下面的雨水道再汇入老街两侧的雨水沟最终流入方岩溪

sections.name: 四、彩画
sections.content_zh: 彩画通常只位于砖墙上端靠近檐口的位置，并随檐口高低起伏，在青砖墙上形成了一个一尺左右的装饰带。由于风雨的侵蚀，能完整保留至今的彩画很少，老街上保留最完整的彩画要属程振昌旅店里照壁上的挂落式彩画。这套彩画分"三开间"，中间绘有垂莲柱、雀替等建筑构件，每一"开间"分成有韵律一些片段，每段独自为题。彩画的主题包括田园茅舍、鸟兽花草等。色彩以黑白为主，辅以少量的靛青和赭石。
sections.content_en: Painted decoration is usually only located at the upper end of brick walls near the eave, following the ups and downs of the eave, forming a decorative band of about one chi on the blue brick walls. Due to erosion by wind and rain, very little painted decoration has been completely preserved to this day; the most completely preserved painted decoration on the old street belongs to the hanging-falling style painted decoration on the screen wall inside Cheng Zhenchang Inn. This set of painted decoration is divided into "three bays," with architectural components such as hanging lotus columns and sparrow brackets painted in the middle; each "bay" is divided into rhythmic segments, each with its own theme. The themes of the painted decoration include rural thatched cottages, birds and beasts, flowers and plants, etc. The colors are mainly black and white, supplemented by a small amount of indigo and ochre.
